guide.title: Medical Terminology
guide.lead: Medical words are built from parts: prefix, root and suffix. Learn the common parts and you can decode most words you'll hear. On the radio and in your report, though, plain language and approved abbreviations keep patients safe.

sections.title: Directions and positions
rows: Closer to / farther from the trunk
Sitting up; semi-Fowler's is partly reclined
notes: Planes: sagittal (left and right), frontal or coronal (front and back), transverse (top and bottom).

sections.title: Abbreviations
items: Use only your service's approved list
Write "units" in full, never U or IU
Leading zero always (0.5 mg); no trailing zero (1 mg, never 1.0 mg)
If in doubt, write it out

quiz.q: The transverse plane divides the body into:
quiz.explanation: Frontal: front and back; sagittal: left and right.

options: An incision through the cricothyroid membrane to make an airway
An opening in the trachea below the cricoid

flashcards.question: Parts of a medical word
flashcards.answer: Prefix, root, suffix (often joined by a combining vowel).

flashcards.question: Proximal
flashcards.answer: Closer to the trunk: the elbow is proximal to the wrist.

flashcards.question: Plane that divides front from back
dys-
flashcards.answer: Difficult, abnormal or painful: dyspnoea, dysphagia.

critical.scenario: A nurse hands over: 'Two days of dysuria, pyrexia, acute confusion; history of CKD stage 3, CHF, type 2 DM; on furosemide, metformin, lisinopril.' Your new partner whispers that they understood half of it.
critical.question: Best action?

options.t: Ask about any term you're unsure of; recognise the key ones (kidney disease, heart failure, diabetes) and what they mean for your care
Nod and look it up later

options.f: You need to act on it.

options.t: Tell your partner to study later

critical.explanation: Urinary infection with confusion in an older adult: think sepsis.
critical.kpi: Interprets medical terminology in a clinical handover

critical.scenario: A man fell from a ladder with a deformity halfway between his left elbow and wrist. You radio the hospital.
critical.question: Most precise description?

options.t: "Deformity of the left forearm, distal to the elbow and proximal to the wrist"

critical.explanation: Add pulse, movement and sensation below the injury.
critical.kpi: Uses anatomical terms to describe injury location

critical.scenario: Your report reads: '68 y/o F c/o SOB x 2 d. Hx COPD, HTN. SpO₂ 88% RA. Tx: O₂ 4 LPM NC, BVM.' A colleague can't interpret several abbreviations.
critical.question: Which principle does this highlight?

options.t: Use abbreviations sparingly and only from your service's approved list

critical.explanation: If in doubt, write it out.
